rawOutput.title: Personal Finance Fundamentals
rawOutput.topic: Budgeting, credit, debt, interest, and index-fund investing
rawOutput.rationale: This sequence develops practical personal-finance foundations from budgeting through investing. It begins with a brief budgeting framework, then teaches interest before credit and debt because those decisions depend on understanding borrowing costs. Investing follows after cash-flow and debt foundations. Later sessions shift to application and retrieval. Sessions fit the available Monday, Wednesday, and Saturday windows and use focused tasks with support adjusted from actual attempts.

sessions.title: Build a Working Budget
sessions.objective: Turn income, essential costs, flexible spending, and savings into a usable monthly plan.
sessions.amountLabel: One monthly cash-flow model and one budget adjustment
completionEvidence: Classify sample expenses into useful budget categories
Construct a balanced monthly budget from sample figures
Explain one adjustment for handling a monthly shortfall

sessions.title: Understand Interest and Borrowing Cost
sessions.objective: Calculate simple borrowing costs and recognize how rates and repayment time affect total cost.
sessions.amountLabel: Two interest calculations and one borrowing comparison
contentTargets: Principal, interest rate, term, and payment
completionEvidence: Calculate interest from a principal, rate, and time period
Compare two borrowing offers using APR and total cost
Explain why a longer repayment period can cost more

sessions.title: Use Credit Responsibly
sessions.objective: Understand credit reports, credit scores, card statements, and behaviors that affect credit health.
sessions.amountLabel: One credit-statement walkthrough and one credit decision
contentTargets: Credit reports and common score factors
Credit-card statement fields and due dates
completionEvidence: Explain how payment history and credit utilization can affect credit
Classify key fields on a sample credit-card statement
Apply responsible credit practices to a short scenario

sessions.title: Create a Debt Repayment Strategy
sessions.objective: Organize debts and compare repayment approaches without losing essential financial stability.
sessions.amountLabel: One debt inventory and one repayment sequence
contentTargets: Debt balances, rates, minimums, and delinquency risk
completionEvidence: Construct a debt inventory from a sample case
Compare two repayment sequences
Explain why minimum payments and emergency reserves still matter

sessions.title: Apply Budget, Interest, Credit, and Debt Skills
sessions.objective: Retrieve the core rules and make a defensible plan for a realistic household scenario.
sessions.amountLabel: One integrated borrowing and repayment case
contentTargets: Repair of gaps exposed by the scenario
completionEvidence: Recall the main factors that determine borrowing cost
Solve a combined budget and debt scenario
Draft a justified repayment recommendation

sessions.title: Learn Investing Foundations
sessions.objective: Connect risk, return, diversification, time horizon, and fees to long-term investing decisions.
sessions.amountLabel: One risk-return comparison and one diversification explanation
contentTargets: Risk, return, volatility, and time horizon
completionEvidence: Compare saving and investing for short-term and long-term goals
Explain how diversification reduces concentration risk
Apply time-horizon reasoning to a sample goal

sessions.title: Understand Index-Fund Investing
sessions.objective: Explain how index funds work and evaluate basic fund information without attempting to predict markets.
sessions.amountLabel: One index-fund comparison and one basic allocation draft
contentTargets: Indexes, index funds, and exchange-traded funds
Expense ratios, diversification, and basic asset allocation
completionEvidence: Explain how an index fund tracks a market index
Compare sample funds using diversification and expense ratios
Construct a simple hypothetical allocation for a stated time horizon

sessions.title: Build an Integrated Personal Finance Framework
sessions.objective: Combine budgeting, credit, debt, and investing principles into an ordered decision process.
sessions.amountLabel: One cumulative case and one personal action framework
contentTargets: Priority ordering across cash flow, debt, and investing
completionEvidence: Solve a cumulative personal-finance scenario
Construct an ordered framework for budgeting, debt management, and investing
Explain and correct any weak reasoning revealed by the case
